name: The Null Garden

description: The Null Garden appears as a sphere of soft, deadly light—the glow of continuous annihilation as stray atoms of interstellar hydrogen meet their antimatter counterparts at the boundary. The light is beautiful, a gentle luminescence that belies the absolute destruction occurring at its surface. Within the sphere, sensors detect antimatter in concentrations that should be impossible to maintain—positrons, antiprotons, and antihelium in quantities sufficient to power a civilization or destroy one.

The boundary is absolute. No known material can survive contact; the annihilation is complete and instantaneous. Ships maintain minimum distances of 10,000 kilometers, where radiation levels are merely dangerous rather than immediately lethal. The pocket itself is stable—whatever mechanism creates and contains the antimatter maintains perfect equilibrium, preventing the explosive expansion that physics would predict. This stability is itself a mystery; by all known laws, the Null Garden should have annihilated itself and everything within light-years microseconds after forming.

The origin of the Null Garden is perhaps the greatest mystery in modern physics. Antimatter cannot naturally accumulate—it annihilates on contact with the matter that comprises everything else in the universe. Something created this pocket and something maintains it, yet no evidence of artificial construction has been found. Theories range from exotic cosmological phenomena to deliberate creation by unknown entities. The possibility that such pockets could be manufactured is simultaneously the most exciting and terrifying prospect in modern science.

Despite the obvious dangers, the Null Garden represents an energy source of unprecedented potential. Controlled harvesting of antimatter from the boundary—using magnetic containment fields to capture antiparticles before they annihilate—has created a small but lucrative industry. The fuel produced here powers the fastest ships in known space, worth more per gram than any other substance. Military vessels guard the harvesting operations carefully; in the wrong hands, antimatter from the Null Garden could devastate worlds. In the right hands, it already has.
